newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hanoi approves record $8.8 bln FDI projects in '96.
newsitem.headline: Hanoi approves record $8.8 bln FDI projects in '96.

text.p: Vietnam's Ministry of Planning and Investment approved foreign investment projects worth a record $8.815 billion in 1996, a rise of around 17.5 percent from the previous year, the official Vietnam News Agency said on Friday.
VNA said the ministry licensed 326 joint venture and wholly foreign-owned projects with capital from abroad and approved applications for 128 existing projects to increase their capital.
That took the number of foreign-invested projects now licensed to 1,633 and their total capital to $28.4 billion.

Hanoi issued a raft of licences in the closing weeks of 1996, including two major urban development projects, confounding expectations that foreign investment would be much lower than the year before.

Disbursement of funds earmarked for investment in 1996 was $2.5 billion, a year-on-year increase of 25 percent. Despite that rise, less than 30 percent of the total capital approved has so far been disbursed.

VNA said Singaporean firms were the biggest investors in Vietnam last year, with 32 projects valued at $2.76 billion in total. Companies from Hong Kong and South Korea were next, while investment from Japan dropped to sixth place from third.
Investment by American firms in 1996 -- a total 12 projects worth $93 million -- put the United States in thirteenth place.
Hanoi, Vietnam's capital, attracted the most investment, with 46 projects valued at $2.622 billion, while 69 projects worth $2.1 billion were approved in Ho Chi Minh City.
